paper.title: GaitSpan: Growing Humanoid Locomotion from Walking to Running
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-07-13; official project page checked 2026-08-30

decision_relevance.why_admitted: It supplies an executable event-level reward family for dynamic locomotion and a soft composition mechanism worth translating into an oracle hypothesis, while its ablations expose why controller-changing and reward-changing interventions must be separated.
not_evidence_for: A reward-only or oracle-only gain under Sam's fixed trainer
An external reference-dataset oracle or OGMP state machine
A recursive agentic harness or continual reseeding loop
A causal benefit from H-SLIP alone across the full command range
Compatibility with an arbitrary foundation controller that lacks the required phase and seed-policy interfaces

mechanisms.name: Frozen-seed residual expansion
mechanisms.description: A frozen walking policy generates structured base actions; a trainable residual adds state- and command-dependent corrections before joint-target clipping.

mechanisms.name: GaitWave hierarchical rhythm composition
mechanisms.description: The same frozen seed is queried under multiple sinusoidal phase scales, and a command-conditioned 2/4/8-bin memory softly composes the resulting action waves.

mechanisms.name: H-SLIP dynamic-stride reward
mechanisms.description: Three virtual-leg levels reward contact-conditioned compression and rebound, controlled touchdown, and flight, with rebound gated by command tracking and an added stance-slip penalty.

mechanisms.name: Self-anchored expansion regularization
mechanisms.description: Low-speed seed anchoring, residual compactness, phase-bin self-similarity, and temporal action consistency preserve walking structure while new gaits are learned.

parameters.name: anchor_coefficient_target
parameters.context: Regularization target corresponding to the four phase scales, stronger at low velocity.

parameters.name: high_speed_sampling_bias_schedule
parameters.context: Linear ramp over the first 95% of training.

parameters.name: actor_critic_entropy_learning_rate
parameters.context: FastSAC actor, critic, and entropy learning rates.

parameters.name: selected_reward_weights
parameters.units: weight in per-step sum w_i * dt * r_i
parameters.context: General reward table; negative posture and regularization terms are separately tabulated.

parameters.name: robot_configurations
parameters.context: Five configurations across three humanoid families.

failure_modes.name: Seed coverage bottleneck
failure_modes.description: A weak or narrow walking seed constrains the behavior family that can emerge.

failure_modes.name: One-step growth only
failure_modes.description: The study expands walking once into jogging/running-like behavior; it does not fold learned behavior back into a new seed or test closed-loop recursive growth.

failure_modes.name: Single-component imbalance
failure_modes.description: GaitWave alone yields limited flight and weak extreme-speed expressiveness; H-SLIP alone produces flight but sharply degrades OOD command tracking.

failure_modes.name: Coarse or hard composition failure
failure_modes.description: A global coefficient predictor leaks high-speed deviations into walking, while hard command partitions cause abrupt boundary artifacts.

failure_modes.name: Fine-tuning overwrites stable walking
failure_modes.description: Direct fine-tuning degrades low-speed behavior without reliably producing sustained high-speed flight; from-scratch variants fail to recover a coherent gait family.

failure_modes.name: Under-specified H-SLIP implementation
failure_modes.description: Equation 2 uses an undefined dynamic gate, while sigma_track, sigma_td, contact thresholds, and several internal event weights are not numerically specified in v1.

failure_modes.name: Evaluation uncertainty gap
failure_modes.description: The paper reports curves and qualitative deployments but does not state evaluation rollout counts, independent training seeds, confidence intervals, or aggregate real-world success.

failure_modes.name: Bundled intervention outside the fixed trainer
failure_modes.description: The reported system jointly changes policy architecture, seed queries, residual learning, objective terms, sampling, and regularization, so it does not estimate either of Sam's two knobs in isolation.

failure_modes.name: Official code unavailable at extraction
failure_modes.description: The official project page linked to LeCAR-Lab/GaitSpan, but that target returned 404 on 2026-08-30, preventing code-level verification.

evaluation.name: Five-configuration Isaac Gym to MuJoCo evaluation
evaluation.description: Policies are trained in Isaac Gym and evaluated in MuJoCo on Booster T1 23/29 DoF, Booster K1 22 DoF, and Unitree G1 23/29 DoF.

evaluation.name: Tracking, flight, and energy metrics
evaluation.description: Tracking error compares commanded and executed base velocity, flight time measures no-foot-contact duration, and energy integrates joint torque-velocity products.

evaluation.name: Seed, multi-expert, and human-demonstration baselines
evaluation.description: The study compares the frozen walking seed, energy-shaped multi-experts, and AMP human-motion priors over in-distribution and OOD commands.

evaluation.name: Component and skill-expansion ablations
evaluation.description: Ablations compare vanilla residual, GaitWave-only, H-SLIP-only, full GaitSpan, scratch variants, direct fine-tuning, and detailed composition/virtual-leg designs.

evaluation.name: Qualitative zero-shot real-world deployments
evaluation.description: The official page shows Booster T1, Booster K1, and Unitree G1 on grass, rocks, gravel, sand, slopes, payloads, and low-friction perturbations, without aggregate outcome statistics.

evidence.locator: arXiv v1 metadata and submission history
evidence.claim: GaitSpan v1 was submitted 13 July 2026 by Kwan-Yee Lin, Zilin Wang, Janelle J. Liu, and Stella X. Yu.
The final action combines composed frozen-seed action waves with a trainable residual and clips the joint target.
GaitWave phase-scales sinusoidal seed observations and softly blends command-conditioned coefficients from a multi-resolution memory.
H-SLIP combines three-level virtual-leg compression/rebound with touchdown, flight, and stance-slip terms.
The total objective combines a standard task reward, H-SLIP, and self-anchored regularization.
The evaluation covers five humanoid configurations, Isaac Gym training, MuJoCo sim-to-sim, and tracking/flight/energy metrics.
Baselines and ablations show complementary tracking and flight behavior for GaitWave and H-SLIP and failures for scratch/fine-tune variants.
The supplement specifies phase scales, anchor weights, memory resolutions, simulator rates, sampling, and FastSAC hyperparameters.
The supplement tabulates general reward weights and domain-randomization ranges.
Self-anchoring comprises low-speed seed proximity, residual compactness, phase-bin prototypes, and temporal action consistency.
Detailed ablations describe global-map leakage, hard-partition boundary artifacts, and shortcomings of one- and two-level SLIP shaping.
Robot-specific configurations include training iterations and embodiment settings.
The authors state dependence on seed quality and coverage and identify one-step rather than recursive skill growth.
